name: memory.admission
description: Admission triage for one RIG Memory OS item (event or knowledge record in unclassified/candidate status). Decides whether it deserves promotion effort, what it is, and the cheapest vehicle -- System-1 triage so the promotion pipeline spends frontier reasoning only where it changes a decision.

criteria.fact: A checkable state-of-the-world claim (config, path, count, version, decision taken)
criteria.lesson: A generalizable procedure or rule learned from a failure or success
criteria.preference: How Mike or an operator wants something done (style, taste, policy)
criteria.activity: Routine telemetry: run records, grade stamps, digests, session noise with no transferable claim
criteria.question: An open thread or intention awaiting an outcome
criteria.sensitive: Personal, credential-bearing, or privately identifiable content that should never be broadly indexed

promote_value.instructions: Value of admitting this item into promoted memory, judged by whether a future agent session would act better because it was retrievable
criteria: Nothing would change; retrieval would add noise
Mildly useful color; sessions would manage without it
Useful once: answers a specific future question
Repeatedly load-bearing: prevents a known mistake or encodes a standing preference
Durable doctrine: changes how multiple future sessions operate and is expensive to rediscover

is_duplicate.instructions: This item restates something the surrounding corpus or prior events of the same kind already establish

evidence_anchored.instructions: The item cites concrete evidence (paths, hashes, commands, ids, measurements) that a verifier could check, rather than vague assertion

rules.reason: do not admit into the broadly indexed plane; flag for gated handling
duplicate of existing canonical knowledge; admission would dilute retrieval
routine activity noise; the canonical event chain is its home, not promoted memory
admission-worthy -- queue for the promotion pipeline (frontier distillation if needed)
